open_points.subject: Model M04 — PhotoPlacement.source_id
open_points.text: `source_id` is the hash of the source.
open_points.question: What representation of the source is hashed to mint `source_id`: the original file bytes, decoded image content, or the normalized image stored in the Portal binary store?
options: SHA-256 of the original source file bytes
SHA-256 of the normalized stored-image bytes
open_points.default_guess: SHA-256 of the original source file bytes

witness.initial: One project receives two JPEG files with identical visible pixels but different metadata or compression bytes.
events: The deliverer places the first file.
The first file leaves the folder and the second file is observed.
outcomes: Hashing original file bytes gives a new `source_id` and creates a second PhotoPlacement.
Hashing decoded image content gives the same `source_id` and returns the first PhotoPlacement without writing.
witness.observer: The owner sees either two hidden Portal photos or one.

open_points.subject: Model M04 — PhotoPlacement.name
open_points.text: `name` is the source's relative path when it was placed and is not updated later.
open_points.question: Relative to which directory is `name` calculated?
options: Relative to another scan or source-folder base

witness.initial: The connection has root `/object`, photo_subfolder `photos`, and the source is `/object/photos/day/a.jpg`.
events: The deliverer places the source and records PhotoPlacement.name.
witness.observer: Any caller or operator reading the PhotoPlacement sees a different source name.

open_points.subject: Model M04 — PhotoPlacement.size
open_points.question: What quantity does the integer `size` record?
options: An image dimension such as longest-side pixels

witness.initial: A stored image is 180000 bytes and 1600 pixels on its longest side.
witness.observer: Any caller reading the PhotoPlacement sees a different fact about the stored image.
